snapshot.readinessLevel: Moderate — 72 at wake; 40 after the intervals, with 36 h recovery showing. That dip is the session, not a warning.

continue: The easy-run fix is working, and you can see exactly where it started. Your last three easy runs ran 87%, 66%, and 82% of their time in Z1–Z2. Compare that to Jul 14, 20, and 21, which sat at 40%, 38%, and 38%. Same routes, same legs — you just slowed down. Nothing else in this refresh matters as much as that.

Volume is climbing without your recovery complaining. Four-week average went 14.4 → 17.5 mi/wk, and the last 7 days hit 27.4 miles. Acute:chronic load is 1.3, which Garmin still calls optimal, and HRV held Balanced every single day. You absorbed a real jump.

Training status flipped from Maintaining to Productive, and the race predictions followed — marathon 3:43:13 → 3:42:51, 10K 44:24 → 44:11, half 1:40:31 → 1:40:11. Small moves, but they're moving the right way while you add mileage rather than in place of it.

Your quality days are still genuinely hard. Today's 6×3min spent 42% of its time in Z4–Z5, and the Jul 22 tempo hit 48%. That's roughly 24 minutes of real work per session. You're not fooling yourself about intensity.
change: The gray zone is still where your training lives: 49% of the last 30 days. Easy went 35% → 42%, which is progress, but the target is 75–80%. The remaining gray isn't in your hard days — it's in the easy days you haven't fixed yet. Keep pushing the same lever: hold easy days at 128–130 bpm and let the pace be whatever it needs to be.

Long runs are the biggest single block of gray left. Jul 18 ran 89% in Z3 for 9 miles. Jul 25 came in at 66% easy for the same distance, so you've already shown you can do it. Make the Jul 25 version the default: start under 125, take a 60-second walk break whenever HR crosses 132, and accept that the first mile will feel absurdly slow.

Garmin is flagging an aerobic high shortage — your monthly load is 982 low-aerobic, 523 high-aerobic, 648 anaerobic. You have plenty of easy and plenty of hard, and a hole in the middle. Fix it by making your threshold day genuinely threshold, not by adding a third quality day: 4 × 8 min @ ~6:55–7:05/mi with 2 min jog, held at 152–158 bpm. Add one interval every two weeks, not more pace.

Watch HRV over the next week. Weekly average drifted 57 → 53 across the last ten days while load ratio climbed to 1.3. It's still Balanced and still well inside normal, so this isn't a reason to back off today — it's the number that tells you whether the ramp to low-20s mi/wk is one you can keep. If it drops under 48 for three straight days, cut the next week's mileage by 20% and keep the quality day.

Sleep is the weak input now, not training. Your Garmin seven-day average is 73 with two nights under 61, and the ring agrees the floor is inconsistent rather than the ceiling low. On the nights you slept 8+ hours you scored 82 and 89. You don't need better sleep habits so much as more of the same ones — protect the bedtime on the two nights a week that slip.
